transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-20
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Lin (Redwood AE), Ethan Moore (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (DataWave - Head of Search), Aisha Khan (DataWave - CTO), Ben Cho (DataWave - ML Eng)

Summary:
- Short hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance.
- Discussed integration options, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security questions (SOC 2, SSO, KMS).
- Agreed next steps: share pricing, benchmark template, and run a 1-week pilot.

Topics: embeddings, reranking endpoint, search relevance, vector store, batching, latency, hosted vs dedicated, security/compliance.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, appreciate you squeezing this in. I'm Sophie from Redwood, I'm the account lead here, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:10] Marco: Good, thanks. Sorry for the slight delay, just wrapping up a stand-up.
[00:14] Aisha: Hi, yes, thanks. We are excited — search relevance has been a pain point.
[00:18] Ben: Hey, hi. Looking forward to seeing the rerank flow.
[00:22] Ethan: Great. Quick agenda: 1) quick context from DataWave on current infra and goals, 2) live demo of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, 3) Q&A on latency/cost/security, 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:34] Marco: Sounds perfect. We'll do a quick 2 minute context.
[00:37] Marco: Right now we run a hybrid infra — Postgres for metadata, Elastic for full text, and a small vector index via Pinecone in a separate service. We've seen issues where the semantic layer sometimes outranks exact matches when we shouldn't, and there are a bunch of edge queries that degrade. We want a consistent reranker to blend signals and to centralize inference — ideally hosted to avoid ops for the pilot.
[01:03] Sophie: That's helpful. Do you have traffic numbers? QPS, typical query latency targets?
[01:08] Marco: Peak search QPS around 120, p95 latency target for search results around 250 to 300ms end-to-end. The current vector lookup plus rerank takes ~600ms p95 in production, so that's the problem.
[01:20] Ethan: Got it. For this call we'll demo our hosted embeddings endpoint (embed text -> 1536-d vector) and our rerank endpoint which accepts candidate doc list + embeddings and returns relevance scores or reordered results. We'll also show batching and continuous prefix cache settings that can help with p95.
[01:36] Ben: Quick question: are your embeddings compatible with our existing Pinecone vectors? Can we re-use them?
[01:42] Ethan: Good question — yes, you can store Redwood embeddings in any vector store. The dimension and vector format are standard floats; you can dump existing vectors in Pinecone and query with Redwood embeddings. There might be small differences across model families for quality but it's interoperable.
[01:58] Aisha: When you say rerank endpoint, is that server-side reordering or do you expect we do candidate scoring client-side?
[02:04] Ethan: You can do either. Our typical pattern: 1) embed query, 2) vector search to get N candidates, 3) call our reranker with the query + candidates. The reranker can return a score or a new ordering and it's all served via the hosted API so you don't need to host a separate model.
[02:20] Sophie: We'll jump into a demo now, Ethan will share his screen.
[02:24] [screen share starts]
[02:29] Ethan: Ok, I'm in the Redwood Console — here's the API playground. I'll show a quick tokenized example and then a real sample from a DataWave-ish dataset. First, embedding endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with text payload, response returns vector. Note: slight transcription here, the SDK naming in the console shows 'embeds.create' but in some examples you might see 'embeddings.create' depending on SDK version.
[02:52] Marco: We use Node on the backend, is the SDK straightforward?
[02:56] Ethan: Yes, Node, Python, and Go SDKs — one-liners to call embeddings. We'll paste a Node snippet in the chat after.
[03:04] Ethan: Now, rerank endpoint — this is the key. You pass in query text, plus candidate documents (or candidate ids + embeddings), and we return scores. The model supports both dense + sparse signals if you want to include BM25 scores.
[03:21] Ben: How do you pass BM25? Do we compute it locally and include as a feature?
[03:25] Ethan: Exactly, you compute the candidate list with whatever retrieval you use (Elastic/BM25), include those scores in the payload as "features" — the reranker uses them along with embeddings to produce a hybrid score.
[03:36] [04:00] Ethan: I'm going to run a sample where query is "how to reset password in enterprise portal" — you'll see the top 5 candidates from our demo index, then we'll call the reranker: call takes ~30-60ms in this demo environment for a single call.
[04:16] Marco: That's promising. Is that consistent at scale? Our concern is p95 spikes when QPS jumps.
[04:22] Ethan: In hosted we provide autoscaling and concurrent request handling; for production p95 you can either go hosted with a multi-slot plan or move to Dedicated if you want predictable throughput. Hosted tends to have variable latency under burst loads but we provide SLOs and smart routing to handle it.
[04:39] Aisha: Do you support per-route concurrency limits? For example, if the rerank is heavy we want it to not block embeddings for chat.
[04:46] Ethan: Yes, per-route config and per-api-key quotas. You can route rerank calls to dedicated capacity while keeping embeddings on hosted if that helps.
[04:54] Ben: On data: we need to keep logs from pilot for analysis but we can't ship raw user text. How does Redwood handle data retention?
[05:00] Sophie: By default hosted API does not retain PII but for enterprise we have options: redact, mask, or configure zero-retention. We also offer Private deployments for full control. We are SOC 2 compliant and can sign DPA; we support SSO/SAML and customer KMS for key management. We'll include the security pack in the follow-up.
[05:20] Marco: Good. Can you share numbers on token cost for rerank vs embeddings?
[05:24] Sophie: Pricing varies by model and feature set. For embeddings it's per-embedding call and for rerank it's per-request + token count if the reranker uses context. We'll send a pricing sheet but rough example: embedding call $0.0004 per call, rerank $0.003 per candidate set (these are demo numbers).
[05:41] Ethan: Back to demo — I'm going to show the batching config. If you expect many short queries we recommend batching of small windows, and the runtime uses continuous KV caching for partially repeated prefixes which can reduce work.
[05:57] Ben: Is KV cache the same as K-V cache in some docs? We saw a reference as K-V cash in an earlier PDF — small typo but confused us.
[06:03] Ethan: (laughs) yes, K-V cache — the docs sometimes auto-transcribe weirdly. It's the key-value cache for model attention/key-value pairs so repeated context is much cheaper.
[06:12] Marco: We are trying to keep p95 under 300ms — any recommended config?
[06:16] Ethan: For p95 you want to reduce batch tail latency: small batch sizes, priority lanes for low-latency requests, and prefix cache enabled. Also consider quantized model variants which reduce GPU compute time. For hosted pilot we can provision fast nodes and tune batching to get you closer to 300ms.
[06:33] Aisha: How invasive is integration? We have an existing pipeline: query -> candidate retrieve from Elastic -> vector similarity -> rerank -> final rank.
[06:42] Ethan: Minimal. You'd replace the reranker with our API call. We'll provide code snippets for Node: embed query, call /search/embeddings to get vector, call Elastic to get candidates, pass candidates + embeddings to /v1/rerank, then merge scores. We also have examples for doing this server-side or as a function in our SDK. We'll paste a snippet.
[06:59] Sophie: I just dropped a link in chat to the quickstart and the Node snippet.
[07:03] [07:10] Marco: For the pilot we want to A/B the reranker against our current logic for a week on ~10% traffic. Is that doable on hosted?
[07:18] Sophie: Definitely. We'll help set up canary routing. You can route a percentage of traffic to Redwood hosted reranker and keep the rest on your current system, then compare metrics.
[07:27] Ben: What telemetry do you expose? We need per-request latency, token counts, top failure cases.
[07:32] Ethan: Console has per-route dashboards: p50/p95 latency, tokens, cost, and we provide traces and raw request logs (subject to retention policy). We can also stream events to your SIEM for longer retention if needed.
[07:45] Aisha: On security again: do you support customer-managed keys?
[07:49] Sophie: Yes, KMS integrations for private deployments and hosted enterprise accounts. We'll include the KMS doc in the security pack.
[07:57] Marco: Any limitations on candidate count to rerank? We usually pass top 100 candidates to our internal reranker.
[08:03] Ethan: For hosted reranker we typically recommend 5-50 candidates to keep latency low; 100 is possible but will affect p95. If you need larger candidate sets we can discuss batching the rerank or doing hierarchical reranking where a lightweight model filters to 20 then the heavy reranker refines.
[08:21] Ben: Could you show a real sample payload?
[08:24] Ethan: Sure. Here's the JSON shape — query, candidates array with id, text, optional embedding and bm25_score. Then a flags object for include_text_in_response:true, score_type:"logit" etc. (shows payload on screen).
[08:39] Marco: Nice. How do we measure relevance improvements — typical metrics we care about are NDCG@10, clickthrough, and manual QA.
[08:45] Ethan: Agree. For pilot we'll instrument NDCG and CTR on canary traffic, and do manual review for failure cases. We'll provide an evaluation harness if you want to run offline evals.
[08:55] Aisha: One operational question: if we onboard to hosted and later need Dedicated, how seamless is migration?
[09:00] Sophie: The API surface is identical — models can be pinned and rollouts are config-based. Migration is largely a config and capacity change; we'll help with the migration plan.
[09:10] Marco: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[09:12] Ethan: Watch out for tokenization differences across models if you port prompts; also embedding drift if you change model families — that can affect vector similarity scores. We'll recommend a baseline evaluation to capture that.
[09:24] Ben: On cost: if we rerank 10 candidates for 120 QPS sustained, what's cost ballpark?
[09:30] Sophie: We'll run numbers in the pricing sheet. Offhand, rerank call cost scales with candidate count and complexity; for a quick estimate we'll work with you on the spreadsheet.
[09:40] [09:45] Ethan: Demo wrap-up: I ran the sample and you can see candidate reordering where the reranker boosted more on-document-exact matches when we included BM25. I'll paste the example responses.
[09:58] Marco: This is good. A few quick security asks: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, SAML config.
[10:04] Sophie: We'll attach SOC 2 and pen test summaries. SAML set up is documented and the SE will help during pilot.
[10:11] Aisha: If pilot goes well, timeline to production? We may need Dedicated for predictable SLAs in Q3.
[10:18] Sophie: That's reasonable. Pilot now, evaluate in two weeks, then plan Dedicated procurement for Q3 if the numbers look good.
[10:25] Ben: For pilot dataset, do you need hashed PII or synthetic?
[10:29] Ethan: Hashed or synthetic is best; we can accept hashed IDs + samples of queries. Ben: We'll prepare the dataset and share a CSV.
[10:36] Marco: OK, to recap the next steps: pricing + security docs from Redwood, benchmark template + example payloads, DataWave to share sample dataset and failure queries, schedule pilot starting 2027-04-26.
[10:50] Sophie: Yep, and I'll add follow-up: we'll propose a pilot runbook and a canary routing plan.
[10:58] Aisha: Great, thanks everyone.
[11:02] Sophie: Thank you — we'll follow up via email and link to the security pack and the Node snippet.
[11:07] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K-V cache as K-V cash), occasional speaker label swaps for short utterances. The content above preserves colloquial speech and some small transcription errors as typical with automated meeting transcripts.
